_company_name_en: Isuzu Motors Limited (EDINET-registered English name; JP: いすゞ自動車株式会社)
_company_type_note: Type C assessment: Isuzu has captive finance subsidiaries (e.g. Isuzu Financial Services Australia, newly consolidated H1 FY2026/3), but pre-cutoff disclosure is single-segment ('vehicles, parts and industrial engines') with no business/finance P&L split, and finance receivables are a small share of the balance sheet. Captive-finance debt cannot be reliably separated from pre-cutoff filings, so the DCF runs on consolidated figures and net_debt is consolidated interest-bearing debt minus cash -- a conservative Type C approximation (finance debt stays IN net debt). Documented as a design decision; reclassify when Isuzu's IFRS-era segment split (from FY2026/3) matures.
_current_price_note: TSE raw close 2025-12-30 (last trading day of 2025), yfinance history auto_adjust=False, cross-checked vs adjusted close 2391.21 (difference = post-cutoff dividends). Live price NOT used (2025-12-31 information cutoff).
_shares_note: Verification formula: issued 777,442,069 - treasury 87,522,085 = 689,919,984 outstanding. Outstanding total = yfinance get_shares_full last pre-cutoff observation (2025-12-09), reflecting the buyback announced 2025-05-29 (up to 35,000,000 shares / JPY 50,000mn; 14,313,500 acquired by 2025-09-30 per Q2 FY2026/3 tanshin). The issued/treasury split is derived (outstanding subtracted from the last disclosed issued count); totals cross-check against tanshin share data.
_hist_note: EDINET annual securities reports (J-GAAP; FY2024/3 figures are the restated basis in the FY2025/3 report: revenue 3,404,633 vs originally-reported 3,386,676, OP 281,641 vs 293,086 -- restatement confirmed by EDINET parse of successive yuho). Isuzu adopts IFRS from FY2026/3, so forecast Year 1 maps to IFRS guidance (revenue 3,300,000 / OP 210,000) while history is J-GAAP; definitional gap documented, not material to margins (<1pt). hist_capex = PP&E acquisitions per cash-flow statement (EDINET); FY2025/3 capex from stockanalysis CF (EDINET parser returned None for that year). hist_debt = interest-bearing debt INCLUDING lease liabilities (yfinance), consistent with the Sep-2025 tanshin disclosure of 801.2bn.
_ltm_note: LTM = FY2025/3 annual 3,235,648 - H1 FY2025/3 cumulative 1,536,305 + H1 FY2026/3 cumulative 1,637,309 (Q2 tanshin 2025-11-12) = 3,336,652. Auto-built LTM neutralized because the pipeline's yfinance enrichment uses post-cutoff quarters.
_net_debt_note: Consolidated: interest-bearing debt incl. leases 758,843 (yfinance, FY2025/3) - cash & equivalents 358,711 = 400,132 (net debt, positive). Type C approximation: finance-backed debt NOT separable from pre-cutoff filings, so it stays in net_debt (conservative). Cross-check: Q2 FY2026/3 tanshin shows interest-bearing debt 801.2bn at 2025-09-30.
_risk_free_note: 10Y JGB yield ~2.07% on 2025-12-30 (MOF Japan historical data; Tradeweb December-2025 month-end close 2.07%).
_beta_note: Raw regression beta: 2-year weekly returns vs Nikkei 225, window ending 2025-12-31 (n=109). Template applies Blume adjustment (0.67*raw+0.33 -> ~0.70).
_size_premium_note: Market cap at 2025-12-30: 2439.5 x 689,919,984 = JPY 1,683bn >> 1tn -> 0.0 per template brackets.
_exit_note: EV/EBITDA exit 6.0x: Japanese OEM/truck peer set at 2025-12-30 trades ~4-7x consolidated EV/EBITDA; Isuzu's commercial-vehicle franchise (higher aftermarket share) supports mid-pack. Set independently of the 7203 reference model.
_capex_note: Hist capex/revenue: FY2023/3 3.4%, FY2024/3 4.7%, FY2025/3 4.9%. 4.9% reflects the CV capacity/electrification investment phase; terminal capex/D&A = 0.049/0.047 = 1.04 (within 0.90-1.15).

Base._note: Central estimate: FY2026 OP margin ~6.4% (tariff year, guidance-consistent), recovering to ~7.3% by FY2028 as Thai LCV demand normalizes and price/mix offsets costs.

Upside._note: Thai LCV recovery + North America CV cycle upswing + FX tailwind; OPM toward FY2024/3 restated peak (~8.3%).

Management._note: Y1 = company guidance issued 2025-05-14, maintained at Q2 (2025-11-12): revenue 3,300,000 (+2.0%), OP 210,000 (implied OPM 6.4%, tariff impact -16,000 baked in). Y2+ fade to a conservative recovery.

Downside 1._note: Tariffs persist + Thai demand stays weak + strong yen: flat revenue, OPM stuck at ~5.5%.

Downside 2._note: Global CV recession + yen appreciation to mid-130s: revenue declines, OPM to ~4% (below FY2022/3 level ex-COVID-recovery).

investment_thesis: 1. Commercial-vehicle franchise with a visible tariff-year floor. Guidance maintained all year at OP JPY 210bn despite a disclosed JPY 16bn tariff headwind, and the model's DCF mid of {target_price} sits {upside_pct} versus the {price} close, with the PGM leg anchored by mid-cycle truck margins rather than peak earnings.

2. Balance sheet supports the cycle. Even on a consolidated (finance-inclusive) net debt basis, leverage is modest against ~JPY 380bn of EBITDA, funding the IFRS-era growth capex and the ongoing JPY 50bn buyback without stressing the payout.

3. Thailand LCV and Middle East CV demand are the swing factors; the CV upcycle in emerging markets plus parts/aftersales (a growing share of revenue) gives margin resilience that the market's ~{per} PER does not fully price.
key_risks: 1. FX and tariff persistence: an extended strong-yen / US-tariff regime maps to the Downside 2 path (OPM ~4%), well below the FY2024/3 restated ~8.3% level.
2. Thailand LCV market structural weakness; a failure of the FY2026 recovery to materialize keeps revenue flat and compresses working-capital efficiency.

3. Type C approximation: captive-finance debt is not separable in pre-cutoff filings, so net debt is conservative (finance debt included) while finance profits remain in the DCF flows; directionally prudent but approximate.
